# Phase 0 Research: Version x Lifting Runtime Comparison

## R1. What "already recorded" means, precisely

**Decision**: The target figure is `benchmarks/figures/benchmark_solvetime.png`, generated by
`benchmarks/make_figure.py` from `benchmarks/results/benchmark.csv`. Confirmed directly (not
assumed): it currently plots exactly 2 bars per model (Gurobi barrier+crossover,
cuOpt-shipped-default-current-version-unlifted), sorted by `n_cols`, with a "gate fail" annotation
already built in for any row where `both_feasible` is `False`. This is the figure FR-005 requires
extending — not a new, parallel figure.

**Rationale**: Grounds "beside the already recorded ones" in the actual code rather than guessing
which of this project's several figures the request means.

## R2. Existing data for the six in-scope models (old version, unlifted) — already fast except S85

**Decision**: Read directly from `benchmark.csv` rather than assumed:

| model | n_cols | gurobi_s | cuopt_s (26.6.0, unlifted) |
|---|---|---|---|
| e_coli_core | 95 | 0.0008 | 0.2489 |
| iML1515 | 2,712 | 0.0337 | 3.75 |
| Harvey | 81,094 | 2.82 | 1.67 |
| Harvetta | 83,521 | 3.53 | 1.42 |
| S84 | 685,998 | 40.6 | 24.6 |
| S85 | 874,634 | 52.6 | 509.4 |

**Rationale**: This directly confirms and explains the user's own scoping decision ("rest of the
microbiome models have the same property as S85") — S84 (685,998 vars) is *not* pathological
(24.6s, comparable to Gurobi), while S85 (874,634 vars) is the one that jumps to 509s. The four
excluded models (S9/S15/S23/S83) are all >1,000,000 vars, i.e. past the same threshold S85 already
demonstrates, matching `specs/012-cuopt-native-tuning/research.md` R5's finding that S85's extreme
`[1e-6, 2e5]` conditioning — not raw size alone — is what drives the slowdown. This also gives a
concrete, evidence-based time budget for the sixteen new solves this feature needs (R5): only the
three S85-involving ones (new-version-unlifted, old-version-lifted, new-version-lifted) are
expensive; the other thirteen are single-digit-seconds-to-tens-of-seconds based on this table.

## R3. Which of the sixteen (model, version, lifted) combinations already exist

**Decision**: Of 6 models x 4 configurations = 24 total data points:

- **6 already exist** (old version, unlifted) — every row in `benchmark.csv` already covers this
  (R2) — reused verbatim, never re-solved (spec FR-007).
- **2 already exist** (old version, lifted) — `e_coli_core` and `S85`, from
  `specs/013-cobra-model-lifting/`'s `benchmarks/results/model_lifting/*.json` (confirmed present
  on disk). `S85`'s already-recorded result there is `verified_correct: false` (the amplification
  finding from that feature) — reused as-is, including its failure status (spec FR-008/Edge
  Cases), not re-solved or reinterpreted.
- **16 must be freshly solved**: `{iML1515, Harvey, Harvetta, S84}` x `{old version, lifted}` (4),
  and all 6 models x `{new version, unlifted}` (6) and x `{new version, lifted}` (6).

**Rationale**: Directly implements spec FR-007/FR-008's reuse requirements with an exact,
verified accounting — not "reuse where convenient," a specific list.

## R4. Isolated environment for the newer version — reused, not re-provisioned from scratch

**Decision**: `/tmp/cuopt-26.8-venv` (provisioned in `specs/012-cuopt-native-tuning/`) still
exists and still resolves `cuopt.__version__ == "26.08.00"`, confirmed directly. This feature's
orchestrator checks for it and reuses it; if absent (e.g. `/tmp` was cleared since), it is
re-provisioned with the exact same command already established
(`python3 -m venv ... && pip install cuopt-cu12==26.8.0 numpy scipy`) — never assumed to silently
exist without a check, since `/tmp` is not a durable, committed location.

**Rationale**: Matches spec FR-002's "same two versions already established" requirement and
research R4/R9 from `specs/012-cuopt-native-tuning/` — this feature does not re-derive the
version-isolation approach, it reuses it directly.

## R5. One model-agnostic worker, launched via subprocess, for every new solve

**Decision**: A new subprocess entry point, `benchmarks/_version_lifting_worker.py`, accepting
`--model NAME --lift/--no-lift`, solving exactly one (model, lift-state) combination via
`gpugem.solve(**lp, lift=<flag>, ...)` and printing one JSON result to stdout (last line — cuOpt's
own native logging bypasses Python's `sys.stdout`, same convention already established in
`specs/004-.../`'s and `specs/012-.../`'s workers). Launched with either `sys.executable` (old
version, matching the shared environment every other benchmark depends on) or the isolated venv's
interpreter (new version) — the same subprocess/interpreter-selection pattern
`specs/012-cuopt-native-tuning/run_cuopt_tuning.py`'s `--upgrade-venv` handling already
established, generalized here from S85-only to any of the six in-scope models.

**Rationale**: One worker handles all sixteen new solves (four combinations of
{old,new version} x {unlifted,lifted}, minus the two already covered by R3) via two flags rather
than four near-duplicate scripts — matches this project's established subprocess-isolation
precedent (CUDA contexts are not safely reusable across a long-running parent process handling
many different problem sizes back to back) rather than introducing a new pattern.

**Alternatives considered**: Reusing `specs/013-cobra-model-lifting/benchmarks/
run_model_lifting_validation.py`'s functions in-process for the "old version" combinations only
(no version switch needed there) — rejected for consistency: mixing an in-process code path for
half the combinations and a subprocess path for the other half adds complexity for no real
benefit, and `run_model_lifting_validation.py`'s own functions (`build_comparison`,
`scale_report`) are still reused as library calls *inside* the new worker rather than
reimplemented, keeping the actual comparison/gating logic in one place either way.

## R6. A derived CSV and figure script, never mutating `benchmark.csv`/`make_figure.py` in place

**Decision**: `benchmark.csv` (10 models, confirmed by direct inspection — includes the four
excluded microbiome models too) and `make_figure.py` are left **completely untouched** — this
project's established, tested, already-published regenerate-from-committed-CSV contract for
`specs/002-benchmark-cuopt-gurobi/`'s own artifact stays exactly as it is. A new aggregator
(`benchmarks/aggregate_version_lifting_comparison.py`) reads `benchmark.csv` (unchanged, base data
for all 10 models) plus this feature's new per-model JSON (R3/R5) and writes a **new**, derived CSV
(`benchmarks/results/version_lifting_comparison.csv`) carrying, for every model, the original 2
columns' worth of data plus three new, nullable configuration columns populated only for the six
in-scope models (`NaN` for the other four, exactly as their rows in `benchmark.csv` already are
for everything this feature doesn't touch). A new figure script
(`benchmarks/make_extended_solvetime_figure.py`) reads this derived CSV and writes to the **same**
output path, `benchmarks/figures/benchmark_solvetime.png` — the file a reader actually looks at
gets the richer, 5-bar version for the six in-scope models (2-bar, unchanged, for the other four),
satisfying spec FR-005's "beside the already recorded ones... not a separate figure" at the level
of the artifact a reader sees, while the underlying regeneration pipeline for the original,
narrower `benchmark.csv`/`make_figure.py` pair remains fully intact and independently regenerable,
never placed at risk of being broken by this feature's changes.

**Rationale**: Matches this project's established, tested "one JSON per candidate -> a dedicated
aggregator -> a derived CSV -> a figure script, each independently regenerable" pattern used by
every prior feature in this project, rather than either mutating a previously-published artifact's
own generation code in place (risking a regression to `specs/002-.../`'s own contract) or
inventing a structurally different pattern for this one feature. Reusing `both_feasible`'s existing
gate-fail annotation visual language (already in `make_figure.py`), generalized from one hardcoded
bar pair to a loop over however many configuration columns are present for a given row, keeps spec
FR-004's correctness-marking requirement visually consistent with the original figure rather than
inventing a new convention.

**Alternatives considered**: Directly modifying `benchmark.csv`'s schema and `make_figure.py` in
place (an earlier draft of this research) — rejected once `benchmark.csv` was confirmed to already
serve all 10 models including the four this feature explicitly excludes, and once it was confirmed
this project already has an established, independent "derive a new CSV + new figure script" pattern
for exactly this situation (`specs/010-gurobi-default-benchmark/`'s
`gurobi_default_comparison.png` is itself a derived, separate figure built the same way, reusing
`002`'s own already-published results rather than editing `002`'s own script) — following that
existing precedent is both safer and more consistent with the rest of the project than the
in-place-edit alternative.

## R7. Correctness gate for the new bars — identical definition, no new tolerance

**Decision**: Every newly-solved configuration is graded by the exact same gate already used
throughout this project (`benchmarks.residual.objectives_agree` against the existing Gurobi
reference already in `benchmark.csv`'s row for that model, `feasibility_residual` against that
model's original `S`/`b`, `status == "Optimal"`) — reusing `specs/013-cobra-model-lifting/
benchmarks/run_model_lifting_validation.py`'s `build_comparison` function directly for the lifted
configurations (unlifted configurations use the same three checks, already implemented in
`benchmarks/run_benchmark.py`'s own existing gate logic).

**Rationale**: Spec FR-004 requires the *same* correctness gate, not a new or looser one for this
feature's new numbers — reusing the actual function rather than re-deriving equivalent logic
guarantees this.
